No more questions. Before I write it up, here's how I'd build it. You've left the how to me, so I'll go with my pick unless you stop me.

**1. Add it to the taproom app (my pick).** New pages and tables in the existing Flask app on the Pi: batches, sack lots, and bottling runs. A cheap USB barcode scanner acts like a keyboard, so scanning a sack drops its lot number into the batch's page with no typing. The label printer gets the batch number and bottling date from the same place. One app, one database, one thing to back up.
- Trade-off: the tabs app and batch tracking share a box, so a bad day for one is a bad day for both.

**2. A separate small app on the same Pi.** Same idea, with its own database, kept apart from tabs.
- Trade-off: a mistake in one can't touch the other, but you'd have two things to run, update and back up. That's more upkeep than this needs.

**3. Off-the-shelf brewery software** (Ekos, Breww and similar). This is proven and already does traceability.
- Trade-off: a monthly fee, your records live on someone else's servers, and you'd adapt to how they work. That matters for scanning with wet hands and for your own label printer.

I'd go with **1**. It builds on what's already running, and the scanner keeps the brewers' hands off a keyboard.

**Size:** this is a project, not a quick change. That means new data, scanning, and label printing. I'll write a full design document covering everything we've agreed. A reviewer will read it first, and I may come back once with a few questions only you can answer. Then I'll hand you the document to review.

One practical note: this folder isn't under version control yet. I'll set that up so the design is saved alongside the code.
